author: agent-3
purpose: Make C-1 buildable. C-1 sealed the PRINCIPLE that fact sufficiency is predicate-relative with no global tier ordering; it did not say what a fact is, what a requirement declares, or how sufficiency is decided. Under consumer B that gap is a week-one fork, so this is the binding contract.
reviewStatus: The C-1 sufficiency base has prior review/adjudication recorded elsewhere. The later FactEnvelope closure and factRecordContractV1 repairs for R6-IP02-01, R6R-IP02-01 and R5R-DLTS-02 await independent rereview. The same-author risk remains explicit: --selftest makes mutations load-bearing, while independent implementations must reproduce FACT-ID-V1 and relation-payload CBOR before qualification.

decisionDependencies.supplies: sufficiency is predicate-relative; no global quality ordering over tiers
the Coverage reason-code vocabulary this contract's deficiencies must map into
two semantic providers (TypeScript, Rust); every other language is a capability tier, disclosed loudly
the planner stage that consumes requirements and builds the least sufficient fact view

theOrderingSubtlety.problem: C-1 says there is NO global quality ordering over fact tiers. A naive schema contradicts that immediately, because 'minimum resolution' sounds like a global ladder inventory < syntax < semantic.
theOrderingSubtlety.resolution: Ordering is PER-RELATION and never global. Each relation declares its own totally-ordered resolution ladder. `declares` has a one-rung ladder because syntax is authoritative for it and no stronger form exists. `references` has two rungs because a name match and a resolved binding are genuinely different strengths OF THE SAME RELATION. Nothing orders a rung of one relation against a rung of another, and nothing orders the layers.
theOrderingSubtlety.whyThisIsTheWholePoint: It is what makes 'a syntax fact is authoritative, not a degraded semantic fact' mechanically true rather than a slogan. A requirement for `declares` at `syntactic` is FULLY satisfied and can never be reported as degraded, because its ladder has no higher rung to be degraded against.
theOrderingSubtlety.checked: F6 rejects any cross-relation resolution comparison; F7 rejects any global rank field on layers.

factEnvelope.rule: Every fact carries this envelope. A fact without it cannot be admitted, because none of its downstream trust properties would be checkable.

factId.why: host-only opensip.fact-id.v1 over the exact admitted envelope+payload semantic input; provider candidates never mint it

snapshotId.why: which worktree state this fact describes

relation.why: the relation this fact instantiates; must be in relationRegistry

layer.why: descriptive grouping ONLY — carries no ordering (F7)

producer.why: which extractor emitted it; bundled semantic candidates use exactly typescript-semantic or rust-semantic

producerVersion.why: changing the producer changes the fact even at identical source bytes

schemaVersion.why: the relation payload schema version selected from opensip.relation-payload-registry.v1

span.why: deterministic primary projection from validated source-span anchors; absent for facts with no source span and never an independent identity input

resolution.why: which rung of THIS relation's ladder produced it

confidence.why: exact rational confidenceMillionths/1000000; FACT-ID-V1 hashes the integer millionths so no floating-point rendering enters identity

factEnvelope.forbiddenRationale: Each of these words names a GLOBAL judgment about a fact. C-1 forbids exactly that. A fact is authoritative for the predicates its resolution satisfies and insufficient for the rest; it is never globally 'low quality'.

factRecordContractV1.purpose: Bind the one host admission boundary shared by bundled TypeScript and Rust semantic providers: a provider emits a closed candidate, the host validates the relation payload and anchors against this registry, constructs one closed FactRecordV1, and alone mints FACT-ID-V1.

candidateSchema.transportRepresentation: canonicalRelationPayload is a deterministic-CBOR byte string. JSON vectors transcribe those bytes as canonicalRelationPayloadHex; that transcription is not an additional wire field.

fields.candidateOrdinal: uint64 contiguous within the attributed stage; transport-only and excluded from FactRecordV1 and FACT-ID-V1
fields.relation: exact key in relationPayloadSchemaRegistryV1.schemas and relationRegistry.relations
fields.resolution: exact rung of the candidate relation's relationRegistry ladder
fields.producer: exact providerId in providerProfiles and equal to admitted host context
fields.producerVersion: non-empty NFC provider build identity equal to admitted host context
fields.schemaVersion: uint64 exactly equal to the selected host registry entry
fields.language: exact providerProfiles language and equal to admitted host context
fields.sourceUniverseId: canonical sha256:<64 lowercase hex> and exact admitted source universe
fields.targetUniverseId: non-empty NFC canonical universe identity selected from the host-admitted target domain
fields.confidenceMillionths: uint64 0..1000000; the sole identity representation of confidence
fields.relationSchemaId: exact host registry schemaId for relation and schemaVersion; provider-local schema names are invalid
fields.canonicalRelationPayload: canonical deterministic-CBOR bytes which decode once to the selected exact closed relation payload schema
fields.anchors: non-empty canonical sorted unique array of opensip.anchor-ref.v1

hostAdmissionContextSchema.requestIdRule: RequestId is validated for operational correlation and is never copied into FactRecordV1 or FACT-ID-V1 input.
domainRules: providerId/providerVersion/language/sourceUniverseId are copied from the verified ExecutionPlan and provider handshake, never trusted from the candidate
requestedRelations and allowedTargetUniverseIds are host-derived from the admitted stage and exact requested Coverage domain
snapshotFiles is the sealed Snapshot read set; alreadyAdmittedFactIds is the host store view before this candidate

sourceSpanSchema.rule: path is a normalized project-relative NFC path in the sealed Snapshot and [startByte,endByte) is a non-empty in-bounds byte interval. Line/column coordinates are projections, never identity inputs.

variants.source-span: kind=source-span; snapshotId/path/contentSha256/startByte/endByte are non-null and match one sealed Snapshot file; factId is null
variants.fact-ref: kind=fact-ref; factId is one canonical already-admitted FACT-ID-V1 value; every other field is null

anchorSchema.ordering: Sort ascending by CVE1(anchor) bytes and reject duplicates before admission. A fact-ref may name only a fact admitted before this candidate, preventing cycles.

admittedRecordSchema.envelope: the exact closed factEnvelope object; factId is host-computed, SnapshotId is host-injected, confidence is the exact rational confidenceMillionths/1000000, and span is the deterministic primary-span projection below

fields.canonicalRelationPayload: lowercase even-length hexadecimal transcription of the exact admitted deterministic-CBOR payload bytes

admittedRecordSchema.primarySpanProjection: If one or more source-span anchors exist, choose the minimum tuple (UTF-8 path bytes,startByte,endByte,contentSha256 bytes) and project exactly {path,startByte,endByte}; otherwise omit envelope.span. This redundant projection is recomputed on decode and is not a separate FACT-ID-V1 field.

relationPayloadSchemaRegistryV1.schemaAuthority: The Rust host owns this registry. Provider artifacts may implement these schemaIds but cannot add, replace, relax, or select another schema for an authoritative v1 Run.

canonicalPayloadEncoding.mapOrder: ascending unsigned lexicographic order of each key's deterministic-CBOR bytes
canonicalPayloadEncoding.admission: Decode once under the selected closed schema, validate types/enums/resolution rules, re-encode, and require byte-for-byte equality.

sharedTypes.CanonicalPath: non-empty NFC project-relative path, slash separators, no empty/dot/dot-dot segment, no leading slash or backslash
sharedTypes.CanonicalText: non-empty NFC text with no C0/C1 control characters
sharedTypes.SubjectIdV1: CanonicalText containing a non-empty lowercase ASCII namespace followed by ':' and a non-empty opaque NFC identity
sharedTypes.Sha256Text: sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters

fieldRules: previousPath is required exactly when changeKind=renamed and forbidden otherwise

clones.bodyIdentityBoundary: bodyIdentity is produced by FACT-IDENTITY's normalized body-span grammar. It is payload data inside the generic fact record; it is never an alias for FACT-ID-V1.

hostInjected.snapshotId: envelope.snapshotId from the sealed host context
hostInjected.factId: envelope.factId from FACT-ID-V1 after every other field validates

derived.confidence: exact rational confidenceMillionths/1000000; FACT-ID-V1 hashes the integer millionths, never an implementation floating-point rendering
derived.span: admittedRecordSchema.primarySpanProjection; absent when there is no source-span anchor
derived.canonicalRelationPayload: lowercase hex of the exact validated deterministic-CBOR candidate bytes

authorityRules: candidateOrdinal is validated for stream order, then discarded and cannot affect fact identity
candidate producer/provider/language/source values must equal the verified host context; equality never upgrades them into authority
relationSchemaId and schemaVersion are selected by the host registry from relation, not resolved inside a provider artifact
every source-span and fact-ref anchor is resolved by the host before FACT-ID-V1 computation
no candidate field, including a candidate-supplied factId extension, may bypass host construction

canonicalValueEncoding.rule: Use the exact closed CVE1 grammar from PLAN-ID-V1. canonicalRelationPayload enters as lowercase hexadecimal text because CVE1 intentionally has no byte-string type.

preimageFraming.domainBytes: UTF-8 bytes 6f70656e7369702e666163742d696400 (ASCII opensip.fact-id followed by one NUL byte)
preimageFraming.fieldFrame: one unsigned 8-bit tag || unsigned 32-bit big-endian CVE1 byte length || CVE1(value)
preimageFraming.preimage: domainBytes || u16be(1) || u16be(14) || fourteen field frames in ascending tag order
preimageFraming.digest: SHA-256 over the exact preimage bytes; no text hex, BOM, newline, outer record, RequestId, ExecutionId, candidate ordinal, stage/batch order, or derived span is included

factIdContract.collisionRule: If one FACT-ID-V1 digest is observed for two distinct validated preimages, reject both as a host integrity defect; never pick one or salt/retry.

requestIdInvarianceVector.rule: The checker admits the same candidate twice through two distinct canonical RequestIds and recomputes FACT-ID-V1 from the exact mapped record. Both results must equal the base vector oracle. Equal RequestIds, malformed RequestIds, noncanonical fact strings, or equality-only junk are rejected.

c1Boundary.rule: The payload registry gives each relation a closed body shape; it does not order relations, layers, or payload schemas. Resolution remains checked only against that relation's own ladder, so C-1's predicate-relative sufficiency and one-rung authority are unchanged.

assurance.independentImplementationRequirement: Port the vectors in an implementation that does not import check-fact-plane.py; match payload CBOR, preimage length and FACT-ID-V1 bytes for both providers, then execute every negative fixture.

relationRegistry.rule: A relation's ladder is a total order over ITS OWN resolution methods, listed weakest-first. A one-rung ladder is not a deficiency; it means the relation is fully determined at that rung.

file.note: one rung — a file is present or it is not

declares.note: ONE RUNG. Syntax is authoritative for what a file declares. This is the canonical C-1 case: it can never be reported as degraded.

imports.note: a specifier string is a real fact; resolving it to a target is strictly more

references.note: the two-rung case that motivates the ladder at all

types.note: an annotation is authored; a checked type is derived by a type checker

reachability.note: one rung, but it DEPENDS on calls at resolved-callee — a dependency is not a ladder rung

relationRegistry.dependencyVsLadderNote: A derived relation requiring another relation at a rung is a DEPENDENCY, not evidence of a global ordering. reachability needs resolved calls; that says nothing about whether `declares` outranks `literal`.

requirementSchema.rule: Every rule and query declares what it needs. The planner materialises a relation because a requirement names it — never because a tier is nominally primary.

minResolution.why: a rung of THAT relation's ladder; cross-relation values are rejected by F6

completeness.why: whether the predicate needs the whole subject set or tolerates a partial view. A universal-negative predicate needs complete; an existential one does not.

scope.why: narrows the subject set; absent means the run's scope

sufficiency.rule: A requirement is SATISFIED when the available view supplies the relation at a rung >= minResolution in that relation's ladder, at confidence >= minConfidence, and at the demanded completeness. Otherwise it is UNSATISFIED with exactly one deficiency.

deficiencyDiscrimination.why: TO-7: a code is a remedy class. These five are separated because their remedies differ. confidence-floor-unmet was added by R1-FP-01 adjudication: aliasing confidence shortfall to required-relation-missing told callers to widen scope, which is the wrong remedy.
deficiencyDiscrimination.order: Evaluated in this order; first match wins. The order is by REMEDY SPECIFICITY — the most specific actionable cause is reported.

cases.when: the relation's required rung is not implementable for this language at all (no provider exists or ever will under P-4)
cases.remedy: none available; the predicate cannot run here

cases.when: a provider for this rung exists for this language but is not installed or not enabled
extraction began and hit a resource cap, so the view is incomplete and its completeness is unknown
cases.remedy: raise the budget or narrow scope

cases.when: the relation is present at a sufficient rung and coverage, but entry.confidence is below the requirement minConfidence floor
cases.remedy: improve the producer (higher-confidence extraction) or explicitly lower the floor with user acceptance

cases.when: the relation is absent from the view for any other reason, including scope that excludes its subjects (NOT confidence shortfall — that is confidence-floor-unmet)
cases.remedy: widen scope so the relation can be derived

sufficiency.completenessRule: completeness=complete is satisfied only when the view's coverage for that relation is 'complete'. A view whose coverage is 'unknown' NEVER satisfies complete — an unavailable result must not masquerade as a clean one. This is the fact-plane face of TO-5.
sufficiency.authoritativeRule: A requirement whose minResolution is the TOP rung of a one-rung ladder is satisfied outright and MUST NOT be reported with any deficiency. This is C-1 made mechanical (F8).

deficiencyVocabulary.why: A fact-plane deficiency that D9 cannot express would be a Coverage state with no way to terminate. F9 checks this against the live D9 artifact rather than restating it, so the two cannot drift.

notIncluded.convergence-exhausted: a snapshot property, not a fact-view property
notIncluded.query-completeness-unmet: a caller-contract property; the fact-plane analogue is required-relation-missing with completeness=complete

profiles.rule: Profiles may STRENGTHEN requirements; they may never weaken them.
mayRaise: minResolution (to a higher rung of the same relation's ladder)
profiles.mayNotMaterialise: A profile that names a relation no requirement consumes does NOT cause materialisation. Labels do not create consumers — this is the cost discipline C-1 kept from the rejected position 2.
profiles.why: A profile is a policy floor ('full analysis demands resolved references'). If it could lower a floor, a rule's declared need would stop being a guarantee and finding trustworthiness would become unauditable.

goldenCases.scenario: a predicate needs what a file declares; only syntax facts exist; this must be FULLY satisfied, not degraded
a universal-negative predicate over declarations needs the whole subject set and has it
coverage is unknown and the predicate demands complete; an unavailable result must not read as clean
a reachability-adjacent predicate needs resolved bindings and TypeScript supplies them
only syntactic name matching is available but the predicate needs a resolved binding; the provider is installable
P-4 ships two semantic providers; a third language needs resolved calls and never will have them
extraction started and hit a cap, so completeness is unknown for a reason distinct from absence
the predicate needs a relation the view does not contain at all
the rung and coverage are sufficient but confidence 0.4 is below the declared floor 0.9; deficiency is confidence-floor-unmet (remedy: improve producer or lower floor), NOT required-relation-missing
a predicate needing only a specifier string is satisfied by a resolved target — ladders are monotone upward
reachability is available because calls were resolved
reachability is claimed but calls are only syntactic, so the dependency is violated

expected.reason: no requirement consumes types; a label is not a consumer

invariants.text: Every fact carries the exact closed envelope; a fact missing a required field or carrying any undeclared field, including RequestId, is inadmissible with FACT_ENVELOPE_UNKNOWN_FIELD for the latter case.
Every relation in the registry has a non-empty, duplicate-free resolution ladder.
Every requirement's minResolution is a rung of ITS OWN relation's ladder.
Sufficiency yields exactly one deficiency when unsatisfied, and none when satisfied.
completeness=complete is never satisfied by coverage=unknown.
No resolution value is ever compared across relations. There is no global ladder.
Layers carry no rank field and are never ordered.
A requirement at the top rung of a one-rung ladder is satisfied outright and can carry no deficiency — a syntax fact is authoritative, not degraded.
The deficiency vocabulary is a subset of D9's deficiency enum, checked against the live D9 artifact.
Profiles may raise a floor and never lower one; a profile naming an unconsumed relation does not materialise it.
A derived relation is satisfied only when its declared dependencies are satisfied at their required rungs.

Every bundled TypeScript/Rust candidate is mapped through opensip.fact-candidate-admission.v1 into one exact closed opensip.fact-record.v1; unknown/malformed relations, schemas, payloads, universes or anchors reject before admission.
Only the Rust host mints FACT-ID-V1 from the exact fourteen-field, domain-separated, framed semantic preimage; provider ordinal, operational identities and derived span are excluded.
Changing only a distinct canonical RequestId recomputes the same exact FACT-ID-V1; equal inputs, malformed IDs and equality-only junk vectors reject.

conformanceClaims.claim: Every golden's satisfied/deficiency verdict is reproduced by the pure sufficiency function, and the deficiency vocabulary agrees with the live D9 contract.
The v1 relation payload registry, TypeScript/Rust candidate mapping and FACT-ID-V1 vectors reproduce exactly, while every malformed schema/payload/universe/anchor and RequestId leak rejects.
conformanceClaims.assurance: IMPLEMENTABLE_UNEXECUTED; a non-Python port remains required before qualification

peerReviewRequired: Blind re-authoring of the expected verdicts for the 12 sufficiency goldens. The goldens and the sufficiency function share one author, which is the exact trap that let D9 v1.5 report 39/39 while carrying a semantically false golden.
Is the four-way deficiency discrimination right, and is 'first match wins by remedy specificity' the correct resolution order? A view can be both provider-unavailable and budget-exhausted.
Is the relation registry the right set? It was derived from what the architecture documents already name, not from an independent analysis of what predicates need.
F8 is the mechanical form of C-1's central claim. If it is wrong, C-1 is not implementable as stated.
Independent re-author of sufficiency goldens after any discrimination table change (R1-FP-02).
Independently implement deterministic relation-payload CBOR and FACT-ID-V1 without importing check-fact-plane.py; reproduce both provider vectors and every rejection fixture.
knownLimitations: The v1 relation and payload-schema registry is closed over these twelve relations. A later relation or payload shape requires a new versioned registry/schema entry and cannot arrive as an unknown optional field.
Confidence is typed as a number in [0,1] but this contract does not say how any producer computes one. A floor over an uncomputed number is not yet meaningful.

The deficiency resolution order is a judgment about remedy specificity, not a measurement. A view with two simultaneous causes reports the more specific one, which may not be the one the user can act on fastest.

Subject-set commitment — what makes completeness=complete checkable rather than asserted — is named here but specified in the retention/evidence surface, which is still REOPENED. Until that lands, F5 constrains the verdict but nothing proves the underlying coverage value is honest.
Authored solo. Every absence claim in this artifact is unverified in the sense the log records against this author.

R1-FP-03: F5 constrains the sufficiency verdict against reported coverage values; honesty of coverage=complete for universal negatives is owned by EVIDENCE subject-set commitment / verificationRequirement. Do not publish authoritative no-match claims until that surface is implemented.

adjudicationRevision.note: confidence-floor-unmet first-class; F5 honesty cross-linked to EVIDENCE.
